# Rylen Anil - Full Site Context

Rylen Anil is a 16-year-old high school student based in Dubai, UAE. He is a developer, ethical hacker, and Junior Cybersecurity Engineer at C3iHub, IIT Kanpur.

Rylen's work focuses on cybersecurity research, responsible disclosure, cloud security, full-stack development, artificial intelligence tools, Linux systems, ESP32 hardware, and practical student-focused software.

## Public Security Research

Rylen reported vulnerabilities in C-DAC e-Sushrut HMIS to CERT-In on September 1, 2026. CERT-In relayed the organization's fix confirmation on September 18. Three public records were published November 17: CVE-2026-124643 covers insufficient dashboard authentication/session validation; CVE-2026-124644 covers hospital operational counters in anonymous login HTML; CVE-2026-124645 describes a static/predictable value in client-side password hashing. The technical writeup traces the original request/response evidence and decodes all 15 counter fields using the original JavaScript. September 1 captures show active SHA-512 at Bokaro and active SHA-1 at AIIMS Patna. They also contain more than one Bokaro token value, so the writeup does not assert a globally invariant token, independently measured token entropy, a proven freshness policy, successful replay, or account takeover. Public token visibility alone is not treated as a vulnerability, and nonce freshness is not claimed to prevent offline guessing after a complete login tuple is captured. Dashboard and statistics observations are scoped to Bokaro; Patna confirmed the object-string hashing construction. CIVN-2026-0557 credits Rylen for the three CVEs and separately credits Sriharan Mahendran for CVE-2026-124646. Sources and writeup:

https://www.cert-in.org.in/s2cMainServlet?pageid=PUBVLNOTES01&VLCODE=CIVN-2026-0557
https://rylenanil.com/posts/cdac-esushrut-session-token.html

Rylen is listed in the U.S. Department of Justice vulnerability disclosure program's official acknowledgments for researchers who responsibly disclosed valid vulnerabilities. His public announcement was posted on October 5, 2026. The acknowledgment does not disclose the vulnerability type, severity, or affected system. Official source:

https://fb6d331c8f530081fa81e12d81678ff8.responsibledisclosure.com/hc/en-us/articles/1500003305722-Acknowledgments

Before speaking at GISEC, Rylen identified an unauthenticated path traversal in its registration platform. The exposed production configuration contained working SQL credentials. Saved evidence shows database authentication, enumeration of 93 database names, and SQL reads returning GISEC visitor records, payment records, and table counts; enumeration does not establish data access across all 93 databases. Rylen also confirmed that he separately checked the exposed API keys and they worked. The saved Stripe and Tap keys have test-mode prefixes; their exposure by the production application does not make them live-mode payment keys. Rylen reported the vulnerability on August 31, 2026. The GISEC team thanked him, acted immediately on the report, and subsequently confirmed the fix. The writeup includes redacted recordings:

https://rylenanil.com/posts/hacking-gisec-before-speaking-at-gisec.html

Rylen identified and responsibly disclosed a JEE Advanced 2026 candidate/result infrastructure issue involving a publicly listable Google Cloud Storage bucket. The exposure involved result JSON records, admit-card redirect files, and admit-card PDFs. The writeup is available at:

https://rylenanil.com/posts/jee-advanced-2026-cloud-storage-disclosure.html

The disclosure was covered by outlets including Hindustan Times, Deccan Herald, India Today, CNBC TV18, Khaleej Times, Firstpost, NewsX, NDTV, The Economic Times, Free Press Journal, Gulf News, Telegraph India, Asianet Newsable, Shiksha, and Manabadi.

## Projects

- Bucky: Bluetooth Rubber Ducky-style ESP32 project that emulates a Bluetooth keyboard.
- Counseltron: AI-powered virtual counselor intended to provide accessible support for students.
- whisperPairForBruce: Whisper audio and contextual metadata pairing project for Bruce devices.
- SSH Desk: full interactive remote desktop delivered through one SSH session and displayed directly in the terminal.
- configTimeMachine: configuration-file version history and rollback utility.
- Elliot: AI Linux assistant that turns plain-English tasks into terminal commands and monitors command output.

## Technologies

Python, C++, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, Linux, Docker, Git, Arduino, ESP32, AI/LLM tooling, and cloud security concepts.
